sources.gives: Leonardo's rule for branch diameters: the exponent D lies between 1.8 and 2.3 (Eloy 2011, Phys. Rev. Lett. 107: 258101)

the bud model: shadow pyramid depth 4 to 8 cells of about one internode (sec 6), shadow a > 0 and b > 1 left user-defined (sec 4.1), light and tropism weights, a specified shedding threshold (sec 4.4), Borchert-Honda alpha (Fig 7), pipe exponent between 2 and 3 (sec 4.5) (Palubicki et al. 2009, ACM TOG 28(3): 58)
plagiotropic axes carry leaves 'generally arranged in one plane'; orthotropic axes are radial (Barthelemy & Caraglio 2007, Annals of Botany 99: 375-407)

rows.value: 2.0: at a fork, the parent's diameter to the power 2.0 equals the sum of the children's
rows.source: [Eloy] 1.8 < D < 2.3 for real trees; [Palubicki] sec 4.5 'usually between 2 and 3'

rows.value: 6 cell layers; the cell is about one internode (a numeric in shape.py, not a key here)
rows.source: [Palubicki] sec 6: depth 'typically ranges from 4 to 8'. The paper gives a range. 6 is the middle of that range.

rows.value: a bud adds a * b^-q to the shadow q cells below it: a 0.5, b 2.0
rows.source: [Palubicki] sec 4.1: a > 0 and b > 1, 'user-defined', no numbers. The paper leaves a and b user-defined; 0.5 and 2.0 are values chosen for the model.

rows.value: a bud's light is Q = max(C - s + a, 0) with C = 1.0
rows.source: [Palubicki] sec 4.1: C is 'a constant', no number. The paper leaves C user-defined; 1.0 is a value chosen for the model.

rows.value: a bud's base vigour is alpha * Q, where Q is its light: 16.75, in the metamer units of this grower
rows.source: [Palubicki] Fig 7 uses alpha = 2, tied to its own light scale. The paper's alpha does not carry over. Fitting to the reference scans gave 15.5 (redbud) and 18 (sweetgum), and a single value fitted neither; 16.75 is their mean. The window was measured: on both tiny fixtures at apical.control 0.5, alpha from 5.5 to 18.95 keeps the grown tree inside the scale guard (0.5 to 2.0), at heights 0.5 to 1.5 m and seeds 1 to 3, with the shedding of the year's new shoots on; it fails at 5.0 and at 19.0. 16.75 lies inside that window. The window is a bound on a toy tree, not a fit: which alpha suits each real species is a per-species question.

rows.value: each new metamer turns twice. First toward the light: the old direction plus 0.3 x the optimal-light direction, made a unit vector. Then toward the gravity set-point by a sine law: the turn, in radians per metamer, is min(0.2 x sin(gap), gap), where gap is the angle between the direction and the set-point, so a metamer at right angles to it turns the most and the turn never passes the set-point
rows.source: [Palubicki] sec 4.3, Fig 12: only 'small' or 'large'. The paper leaves the weights user-defined; 0.3 and 0.2 are values chosen for the model. The sine-law turn toward the set-point is a model choice with no citation. The light and gravity weights are not tuned to make any test pass.

rows.value: a side branch is shed when its light per internode falls under 0.2
rows.source: [Palubicki] sec 4.4 (after Takenaka 1994): 'a specified threshold', no number. The paper leaves it user-defined; 0.2 is a value chosen for the model.

rows.value: a limb stops short of a limb already grown where their gap falls under 1.2 x the thinner radius
rows.source: The grower's stop-short rule. The principle is a fact: solid wood cannot pass through solid wood. The 1.2 is a modelling margin, not measured.

rows.value: 1: two-ranked leaves on a plagiotropic (horizontal or slanted) axis lie about in one plane; on an orthotropic (upright) axis they go round it
rows.source: [BC] section 'Orthotropy, plagiotropy and mixed axes': leaves and branches 'generally arranged in one plane' on plagiotropic axes, radial on orthotropic ones

rows.value: two-ranked buds go round the axis within 20 deg of vertical, lie flat past 60 deg, and change smoothly between
rows.source: [BC] states the fact (plagiotropic axes carry leaves in one plane, orthotropic ones radially) but gives no angle. The two angles are a model choice, not measured: they only have to put the flat case on clearly slanted shoots and the round case on clearly upright ones, and a smooth band avoids a jump between them.

rows.value: 1: a deciduous tree carries leaves only on the current year's shoots
rows.source: none: a kit-wide assumption. A search for a dendrology source that says it found none, and some trees carry leaves on short spur shoots of older wood (apple, pear), so it is a constant of the model, not a cited fact.
